Only trust it if you know this is your own server. MailCtrl then accepts exactly this certificate for the account, and nothing else.
%1$s uses a certificate the phone doesn\'t trust: self-signed (like Proton Mail Bridge\'s) or from a private authority.
A notification for each new message
This account sends mail to its server unencrypted. Only use that on your own network or over a VPN.
When you delete an open message
It goes to the Trash folder, or is deleted for good if it\'s already there or the account has no Trash.
What you wrote is deleted from the phone.
Messages you start but don\'t send are kept here. Attachments aren\'t kept in drafts.
Everything in this folder is deleted from the server for good. This can\'t be undone.
This attachment can\'t be found in the message any more
Wrong username or password. Providers with two-step sign-in need an app password.
Can\'t reach the server. Check the address, the port and your connection (or your VPN).

Screenshots and screen recordings show a blank screen

No app on this phone can open that link
As soon as you leave the app
Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening MailCtrl. While locked, your drafts stay encrypted with the PIN and the recent-apps screen hides your mail.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
At least %1$d digits, separate from your phone\'s PIN
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN.
Enter your app PIN to turn the lock off.
A fingerprint was added or removed. Unlock with your PIN, then turn fingerprint unlock on again.
Couldn\'t unlock with your fingerprint. Use your PIN.
Only strong biometrics such as your fingerprint, checked by the phone\'s secure hardware. The PIN is still needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Confirm it\'s you to see your mail
Set up a fingerprint on this phone first

The PIN can\'t be recovered. Confirm it\'s you with your phone\'s own screen lock to turn the app lock off. Drafts encrypted with the old PIN are deleted, and accounts whose password was sealed with it ask for their password again. Your mail stays on your servers.

The PIN can\'t be recovered, and this phone has no screen lock to confirm it\'s you. To start over, clear MailCtrl\'s storage in Android\'s settings and add your accounts again (your mail stays on your servers).
The PINs didn\'t match. Start again.
Enter your PIN. It\'s needed after a restart and every 72 hours.
Use your phone\'s screen lock to confirm it\'s you
Couldn\'t save the PIN. Try again.
Too easy to guess. Try a less obvious PIN.
Too many tries. Try again in %1$d s
Opening a message marks it read on the server too
(This text is too long to show here.)
This account has no Archive folder
No folders yet. Pull down to refresh.
Accounts that are off are never checked in the background.
Sound, vibration and pop-ups, in Android\'s settings
Unrestricted lets Android run checks on time even while the phone sleeps. It costs very little: a check is one short connection per account.
Android may delay checks while the phone sleeps. Tap to allow MailCtrl to run unrestricted.

Android can delay background checks to save battery. With ntfy, whatever watches your mail (for example goimapnotify on your server) wakes MailCtrl the moment mail arrives; MailCtrl then checks and notifies you. The README shows how.
MailCtrl checks your inboxes itself, now and then, and tells you about new mail. Nothing goes through Google or any other push service.
Android can cut ntfy\'s connection while the phone sleeps, so wake-ups arrive late. Tap to open ntfy\'s App info and set Battery to Unrestricted.
Instant notifications come only through the ntfy app. Install it, then turn on Instant with ntfy. Background checks work without it.
Android blocks MailCtrl\'s notifications. Tap to allow them.
Your server wakes MailCtrl through the ntfy app when mail arrives
ntfy couldn\'t register MailCtrl (%1$s). Open ntfy once, then turn this on again.
Needs the ntfy app, which isn\'t installed
On. Give your mail watcher the address below
Posts to the push address, like your mail watcher will, so MailCtrl checks straight away
Couldn\'t reach the push address. Is your ntfy server reachable from this phone?
Sent. “Last wake-up” updates when it arrives.
ntfy temporarily unavailable: its server can\'t be reached. Your address stays the same, and background checks keep running.
Waiting for ntfy to give an address…
The password is needed again. Tap to enter it.
Encrypted with the phone\'s hardware key, so notifications work while locked
Sealed with your PIN: nothing can sign in while MailCtrl is locked
MailCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only connects to your own mail servers.

Notifications are on, so background checks can sign in while MailCtrl is locked: passwords are then only encrypted with the phone\'s secure hardware, as without the app lock. Turn off notifications to seal them with your PIN too. MailCtrl has no analytics or tracking.
Pictures and content from the internet are blocked, so the sender can\'t see that you opened this.
Pictures loaded from the internet tell the sender when and where you opened a message. Pictures sent inside a message always show.
Searches on your mail server, so it finds everything, not just what\'s on the phone.
Try other words, or search another folder.
Not sent: %1$s. It\'s kept in your drafts.
Sent, but no copy could be put in the Sent folder

Providers with two-step sign-in want an app password here instead of your normal password: make one in your account\'s security settings. MailCtrl only signs in with a password (IMAP and SMTP); there\'s no sign-in through a web page.
Fill in both servers and their ports
Sign in with your address and password. MailCtrl talks to your mail server directly: no MailCtrl server, no tracking.
This provider doesn\'t let mail apps in (it has no IMAP), so it can\'t be added.
Check this account for new mail in the background
New password (leave empty to keep it)
Your password is encrypted with a key in the phone\'s secure hardware and only ever sent to your own mail servers.
Enter the address of your hydroxide or Proton Mail Bridge server below.
Proton Mail is read through hydroxide or Proton Mail Bridge running on your own server. Enter its address under Servers (over your VPN), and the password it gave you, not your Proton password.
Turn off for servers that do it themselves (otherwise sent mail shows up twice)
Your name (shown to people you write to)
%1$d certificate(s) you trusted for this account
With “None”, your password and mail travel unencrypted. Only use it for a server on your own network or over a VPN, such as hydroxide.
MailCtrl is free and open source. Sponsor development on GitHub
Archive and Delete show an Undo bar for a few seconds.
The Inbox tab can show every account\'s inbox together, newest first. Each account chooses whether it\'s in it
This account needs an app password, not your normal password. Make one in your account\'s security settings (two-step sign-in has to be on), then paste it here.
The provider blocked this sign-in until you confirm it in a web browser. Sign in to your mail on the web, approve it, then try again.
Its mail and unread count are part of All inboxes
Adds your public key to every message you send, so people can write back encrypted
The key signs what you send and is used to decrypt what\'s sent to you. Everything you encrypt is encrypted to it too, so you can read your own sent mail.
Passphrases are only ever kept in memory, and forgotten when MailCtrl locks. Looking up a key asks the recipient\'s own mail domain for it, only when you tap Look up.
Your keys and your contacts\' keys, to encrypt and sign mail
Offer “Look up” for a missing key. It asks the person\'s mail domain, and only when you tap it
This message is encrypted, but not to any of your keys on this phone
The encrypted data is damaged or was changed on the way, so it isn\'t shown
This message was encrypted without an integrity check, so it could have been changed by someone else. It isn\'t shown, to keep you safe.
That\'s too big to handle on the phone
There\'s no valid key to encrypt to
Your key can\'t sign: it has expired, was revoked, or has no signing key
This account has no OpenPGP key. Pick or make one in the account\'s settings, or turn Encrypt and Sign off.
Your key is locked: enter its passphrase to sign
No key to encrypt to for %1$s
Your own key can\'t be encrypted to (it has expired or was revoked)
Open the message again to decrypt this attachment
Your secret keys stay on this phone, encrypted with its secure hardware and protected by their passphrase. Only public keys can be shared.
A public or secret key, armored (.asc) or binary (.gpg, .pgp)
Keys come from files, attachments, the Autocrypt header of a message, or a lookup. Compare the fingerprint with the person before you rely on a key.
Look up a key by address
Asks that address\'s mail domain (Web Key Directory)
To be sure a key is really theirs, compare this with the fingerprint the person reads out to you.
No passphrase: anyone with this phone unlocked can use it
An account signs with its key and is encrypted to it. One key per account.
This is your secret key. Without it, mail encrypted to it can\'t be read on this phone any more, and this can\'t be undone.
You can\'t encrypt to this person or check their signatures until you import their key again.
Your key is made on this phone and never leaves it; only its public part is shared. Curve25519 is small and fast, and what GnuPG, Thunderbird and Proton make too.
The passphrase can\'t be recovered. Without it, mail encrypted to this key can\'t be read.
Making your key… An RSA key can take a minute.
You already have a different key for this address. Only import this one if you know the person changed their key.
Compare the fingerprint with the person before you rely on this key.
No OpenPGP key in this file
MailCtrl will ask %2$s for the key of %1$s, over HTTPS. That tells %2$s that someone looked this address up, from your connection.
Decrypted on this phone. Only you and the recipients can read it.
Encrypted to your key %1$s. Unlock it with its passphrase to read the message.
The key is for %1$s, not the sender\'s address
The key has expired or was revoked, or isn\'t meant for signing
Key %1$s isn\'t on this phone, so the signature can\'t be checked
This message was changed after it was signed, or the signature is forged
The sender\'s key is in this message
You have a different key for this address
Encrypted to every recipient\'s key, and to yours
You\'re quoting an encrypted message without encryption.
